/itineraryStops/2/smartNotes/tip.source_en: Hire a free volunteer guide at the entrance for cultural context; respect that residents actually live here — don't enter homes uninvited

/itineraryStops/2/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Visitor information center at entrance; English maps available

/itineraryStops/2/whyOnRoute.source_en: **The day's only inland Joseon-era heritage site and its geographic pivot point.** Located on the way from the Hamdeok coast toward Seongsan (inland Pyoseon), it turns plain driving time into a meaningful stop. The stone walls and thatched roofs of this National Folklore Cultural Heritage village and its 600-year-old old trees add a 'leisurely cultural walk' that contrasts with the afternoon's volcanic and haenyeo heritage, balancing the day so it is not just a pilgrimage of photo spots.

/itineraryStops/2/description.source_en:
**⟦G0⟧ (성읍 민속마을)** is an inhabited Joseon-era village that preserves old Jeju stone walls, thatched-roof houses, narrow alleys, and traditional household layouts. Historically, the village served as the administrative center of Jeongui-hyeon, one of the main local districts of Joseon-era Jeju, and its heritage value is recognized as an Important Folklore Cultural Heritage site. 

Unlike a staged folk park, people still live here, so the visit must be respectful and quiet around private homes. The village is also known for its old zelkova and hackberry trees near the center, traditional Jeju architecture, and local stories about daily life in a windy volcanic island environment. 

For visitors, this stop gives a grounded cultural contrast after Hamdeok's coast: guests see how Jeju people historically built homes, protected villages with stone walls, and adapted to a harsh island climate.

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Easy — flat dirt and stone paths through the village

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/admission.source_en: Free for general village; some private homes charge for guided visits

/itineraryStops/3/highlights/5.source_en: Group dietary requirements collected at pickup

/itineraryStops/3/whyOnRoute.source_en: **A recharge right before the core UNESCO itinerary.** At a local restaurant on the road from Seongeup to Seongsan, you have lunch of eastern Jeju local fare such as black pig, abalone hot pot, and seasonal seafood (meal not included). It is the spot to fill up before the most active afternoon — climbing Seongsan, the haenyeo diving performance, and Manjanggul.

/itineraryStops/3/description.source_en: About a 60-minute lunch break between ⟦G0⟧ and ⟦G1⟧. At restaurants around Seongsan-eup harbor you can explore eastern Jeju local fare such as black pig, abalone hot pot, and cutlassfish. Lunch is not included (about ₩15,000).

/itineraryStops/4/category.source_en: UNESCO Tuff Cone — Sunrise Peak (Triple UNESCO Designation)

/itineraryStops/4/timeUsed/1.source_en: Ascent to summit deck (0.8 km / 140 m gain) — ~30 min

/itineraryStops/4/timeUsed/2.source_en: Summit views + crater rim photos — ~20 min

/itineraryStops/4/timeUsed/4.source_en: Optional haenyeo viewing at base (14:00 show; may be canceled in bad weather) — ~10 min

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/0.source_en: **Triple UNESCO**: World Heritage 2007-07-02 + Biosphere Reserve 2002 + Global Geopark 2010-10

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/1.source_en: **5,000 years old** — Surtseyan-type hydrovolcanic eruption, magma-meets-seawater steam-explosive birth

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/2.source_en: Crater **600 m wide × 90 m deep**, ringed by **99 jagged rim rocks** (the 'stone crown')

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/3.source_en: **182 m above sea level** — 0.8 km / ~140 m gain, 60-min round trip on stone-step trail

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/4.source_en: **18 Imperial Japanese WWII caves** at base — 1945 kamikaze suicide-boat shelters

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/5.source_en: **Haenyeo demonstration once daily at 14:00 (subject to bad-weather cancellation)** at the seaside cove — UNESCO Intangible 2016

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/6.source_en: **Admission updated April 2025**: Adult ₩5,000 / Youth ₩2,500 / FREE under 7 + over 65

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/8.source_en: **Closes for first Monday of each month** (occasional rest day)

/itineraryStops/4/smartNotes/tip.source_en: All stairs but well-maintained — manageable in casual clothes; family-friendly with rest stops; sunrise visits popular but crowds gather pre-dawn

/itineraryStops/4/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Café (Fritz Coffee 1.3km away has best exterior views of the peak); ferry to Udo Island from Seongsan Port (1.5km/15 min walk)

/itineraryStops/4/whyOnRoute.source_en: **The first of the day's two World Natural Heritage sites.** After lunch you climb ⟦G1⟧ (optional climb, about 30 min round trip) to see the tuff cone that rose from an underwater eruption about 5,000 years ago. The climb leads straight into the haenyeo diving performance held in the sea of the same area, then wraps up at the ⟦G0⟧ — part of the same 2007 inscription — completing the 'Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes' narrative in a single day.
